title: relay-run step and end extend a run in a legacy ledger
lead: A run begun before the shared ledger, and so held only in a checkout's `.slicer/relay-runs.jsonl`, can still take `relay-run step` and `end` after an upgrade.
findings_note: s298 relay 2026-10-16: legacy-ledger run lists but step/end give unknown_run
boundary: **Not in this slice:** extending a run that lives only in a sibling worktree's legacy ledger (begin a new run there); moving legacy runs into the shared ledger.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
s298 (landed 2026-10-16) moved the ledger to `<git common dir>/slicer/relay-runs.jsonl`. `list_runs` still reads the old per-checkout files, but `_open_run` (`src/slicer/ops.py`, after s298) looks only in `relayrun.ledger_path(root)`, so a run that was in flight at the upgrade lists yet cannot be extended or ended: `unknown_run`. The s298 relay hit exactly this: its own run sat in the old ledger, and the outer session had to record every step with main's pre-upgrade code. s298 documents "begin a new run" as the workaround.

**Owner decision (open):**
- (a) **Recommended.** `_open_run` falls back to this checkout's `relayrun.legacy_ledger_path(root)`, and the step or end event appends to the file that holds the run, under the project lock. That writes a legacy file, which s298 kept read-only.
- (b) Keep the workaround and retire this item.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: `_open_run` returns the run and the ledger path it came from; `relay_run_step` and `relay_run_end` append there, taking `store.project_lock` for a legacy file and `ledger_lock` for the shared one. `unknown_run` names both paths it read.
- `src/slicer/relayrun.py`: `append` takes the target path.
- `docs/commands.md` (Relay run ledger: remove "begin a new run" for this case), `CHANGELOG.md` under Fixed.
- `tests/test_relay_run.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_RelayRun_Step_RunInLegacyLedger_AppendsThere`: a run only in `.slicer/relay-runs.jsonl` takes a step; the event is in that file, and the shared ledger has no line for it.
- `test_RelayRun_End_RunInLegacyLedger_Ends`: `list` shows it ended.
- `test_RelayRun_Step_UnknownRun_NamesBothLedgers`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the fallback and the per-path append; mutation-check (drop the fallback; append to the shared ledger instead).
3. Run mutations with TMPDIR fixtures that are their own git repos or use `support.isolated_discovery`, and check the real `.git/slicer/` is unchanged before and after.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
